text:
maya: heads-up — seeing intermittent output drift and rare hallucination spikes on awq 3-bit serving for xtl-13b when group_size >= 64. latency tails also spike. anybody else?

jordan: saw something similar on canary earlier today, but thought it was dataset noise. do you have repro steps?

maya: quick notes: reproduce locally with long-context prompts (seq ~ 1500). config: group_size=96, actq=8, per-tensor scales. disabling KV cache seems to reduce frequency but not eliminate. snippet:
```
model: xtl-13b-awq
group_size: 96
activation_quant: 8
kv_cache: enabled
seed: 42
```

sam: hmm. i tried non-uniform group schedules during a dry run (larger groups in first layers, smaller later) and saw fewer drifts. ran 50 prompts from convo-set-2k: ppl delta ~ +0.8% vs fp32, tail latency down ~12%.

lee: could be cache-alignment + rounding bias. when groups change stride for kv cache, index math might round to different buckets — amplification over long contexts. saw logs like:
```
[warn] layer 23: kv_index_mismatch 0.00043
[debug] attn_scale drift 1.2e-3 -> 4.9e-3 after step 120
```

ciara-bot: deploy-canary: xtl-13b-awq group=96 actq=8 -> 3/20 requests failed QA checks (probability divergence) :rotating_light:

jordan: hypothesis: group quantization rounding bias accumulates in attention scores with long contexts. experiments to isolate:
- run with actq=12 and group_size=96
- run with group_size=48 actq=10
- run with per-channel scales instead of per-tensor
- disable kv-caching to see effect on accumulation

maya: i'll kick off two canaries now.
canary-A: group=48 actq=10 (no kv cache)
canary-B: group=96 actq=12 (kv cache ON)
@sam can you run eval harness (2k prompts) with deterministic seed and collect ppl, top1 divergence, entropy spikes? also include median and 95/99 latencies.

sam: on it. running locally with:
```
python eval_harness.py --model xtl-13b-awq --prompts convo-set-2k --seed 42 --store-metrics --canary canary-A
```
ETA ~2h, disabling async batching to isolate.

lee: if we confirm, we should add a runtime fallback rule: if token-level KL divergence > 1e-3 for consecutive tokens, route request to int8-safe variant. sample policy snippet:
```
fallback:
  metric: token_kl
  threshold: 1e-3
  window: 3
  target: xtl-13b-int8-safe
```

maya: added to runbook + opening PR for experiment harness hook to emit token_kl per-request. tagging @eng-runtime for tracing hooks. :spiral_notepad:

(2h later)

sam: results:
- canary-A (group=48 actq=10, kv disabled): ppl delta +0.9% vs fp32, median latency +5%, 95p latency +18%, 99p +28%, tail divergence events: 3/2000
- canary-B (group=96 actq=12, kv enabled): ppl delta +0.3%, median latency +3%, 95p +12%, 99p +40%, tail divergence events: 9/2000
notes: raising actq to 12 helps perplexity but group=96 still produces more tail divergence; disabling kv cache reduced events significantly for group=48.

jordan: useful — looks like actq raise helps quality but doesn't fully fix long-tail instability with big groups and kv ON. next steps:
1) push canary-B (actq=12, group=96) to staging but enable runtime fallback per lee's policy
2) try non-uniform group schedule: larger groups in earlier layers, taper later (e.g., [96,96,64,32,...]) and measure
3) run per-channel scale quantization experiment (may help block-level bias)

devops: created alert rule #342: "awq_token_divergence" -> triggers when token_kl > 1e-3 for 3 tokens, sends to prod-oncall. added to staging as well.

ciara-bot: alert: awq_token_divergence triggered 2 events during staging canary run. linked: https://ciara/reports/342

maya: thanks team. i'll implement non-uniform group scheduler and wire per-channel quant flags into the bakeoff config. re-run tomorrow morning and report. tagging @eng-ml for visibility. :white_check_mark:

sam: optional: we should also try micro-batching alignment (pad to group boundaries) to avoid partial group residuals — could be low-effort to test.

lee: agree. will add padding experiment to the list. good progress.

(reacts: :eyes: from jordan, :thumbsup: from devops)
